acceptance_criteria.criterion: `GET /api/models` returns the model array, auto-initializing `local.json` from defaults on first access
`PUT /api/models` auto-generates UUIDv4 for entries without `id` and persists all entries
`PUT /api/models` with a duplicate slug returns a validation error
`PUT /api/models` with reserved slug `"inherit"` on a non-sentinel entry returns a validation error
`PUT /api/models` removing a referenced model returns 409 Conflict with a list of usages directing the user to the Replace Model feature
`POST /api/models/load-defaults` merges defaults without overwriting existing entries and returns slug-collision conflicts

`GET /api/model-assignments` returns assignments enriched with `stale: true` when `max(mtime(assignments.json), mtime(local.json))` > `mtime(name-mapping.json)`, `stale: false` when neither user file exists, and `stale: false` when only `default.json` is newer
`PUT /api/model-assignments` validates model UUIDs exist in registry and persona keys exist in `name-mapping.json`; returns 400 when `name-mapping.json` doesn't exist

`POST /api/model-assignments/replace` swaps all occurrences of `old_model_id` with `new_model_id`; rejects when `old_model_id` is not referenced (400); rejects when `old_model_id === new_model_id` (400 "Source and target models must be different")
`GET /api/personas` returns all personas from `name-mapping.json` when it exists, or empty array when it doesn't
`POST /api/personas/rebuild` spawns `node scripts/build-personas.js`, returns `{ success: true, output }` on exit 0 and `{ success: false, output, exitCode }` with HTTP 500 on failure
`POST /api/personas/rebuild` returns 409 when a build is already in progress; clears the `buildInProgress` flag on process errors (finally-block cleanup)
All 8 API client methods are added and call the correct endpoints with correct HTTP methods

summary: Created mcp-server/gui/api-models.ts with all 8 handler functions: handleGetModels, handleSaveModels, handleLoadDefaults, handleGetAssignments, handleUpdateAssignments, handleReplaceAssignedModel, handleGetPersonas, handleRebuildPersonas.

handleSaveModels: auto-assigns UUIDv4 via randomUUID() for entries missing id; delegates to writeModels() which enforces slug uniqueness, reserved-slug guard, and deletion guard; returns 409 CONFLICT with referencedModels details when a deletion is blocked.

handleGetAssignments: computes stale boolean by comparing max(mtime(assignments.json), mtime(local.json)) against mtime(name-mapping.json); default.json excluded from comparison; returns stale:false when neither user file exists.
handleUpdateAssignments: validates name-mapping.json existence (400 if absent); validates all persona keys against id values in name-mapping.json; validates all model UUIDs against registry.

handleReplaceAssignedModel: rejects same-model swap with message 'Source and target models must be different'; rejects when old_model_id not referenced; swaps all occurrences including default_model_uuid.
handleGetPersonas: reads name-mapping.json, returns empty array on ENOENT.
handleRebuildPersonas: module-level buildInProgress concurrency guard (409 on concurrent); spawns node scripts/build-personas.js non-detached; captures stdout+stderr; clears flag in finally block.

Registered 3 GET routes in matchRoute() (models, model-assignments, personas) and 5 body-parsing routes in handleRequest() (PUT models, POST models/load-defaults, PUT model-assignments, POST model-assignments/replace, POST personas/rebuild).
Added 8 API client methods to api-client.js: getModels, saveModels, loadDefaultModels, getPersonas, getAssignments, updateAssignments, replaceAssignedModel, rebuildPersonas.

comments.note: server.ts handleRequest() has grown substantially (~1900 lines) and now handles 5 more body-parsing routes inline. The inline body-parsing pattern (repeated try/catch/sendError boilerplate for each route) is functional but verbose. A future refactor could introduce a typed route registry or a dispatchBodyRoute() helper to reduce duplication. Out of scope for this WP but worth noting for maintainability.

api-models.ts handleRebuildPersonas() uses a non-typed Promise wrapper around spawn() events. The pattern is correct and mirrors orchestrator-manager.ts, but a typed utility wrapper (e.g. spawnWithOutput(cmd, args, cwd): Promise<{output, exitCode}>) shared between the two callers would eliminate duplication if a third caller appears.

handleUpdateAssignments() reads both name-mapping.json and local.json in sequence. Both reads are independent and could be parallelized with Promise.all() to reduce latency for users with large registries. Minor optimization opportunity.

The _resetBuildInProgress() export in api-models.ts uses an underscore prefix to signal 'test-only'. The project doesn't have an established convention for this (api-repos.ts has no test-only exports). A JSDoc @internal tag is present which is sufficient; just noting the minor convention gap.

summary: Reviewed 4 files (api-models.ts, server.ts, src/gui/model-registry.ts, gui/public/api-client.js). 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium (info disclosure in validation error — noted), 1 Info (unconstrained cast in handleGetPersonas). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Medium — A05 (Security Misconfiguration / Information Disclosure). File: mcp-server/gui/api-models.ts, line ~339 (handleUpdateAssignments). The validation error message for an invalid persona key leaks the full list of valid persona IDs: `Valid IDs are: ${[...validPersonaIds].join(', ')}`. In this context the risk is low (GUI is localhost-bound, CORS is restricted, persona IDs are not secrets), but this is an unnecessary detail in an error message. Remediation: emit only the count of valid IDs or a generic message (e.g. 'Persona key X does not exist in name-mapping.json. Run a build to refresh the persona list.') rather than enumerating all valid values.

Info — A04 (Insecure Design / Type Safety). File: mcp-server/gui/api-models.ts, line ~507 (handleGetPersonas). The final return statement `return parsed as PersonaEntry[]` casts the JSON-parsed array to the PersonaEntry interface without Zod validation of individual entry shapes. The file is locally owned (not user-submitted) so direct exploitation risk is minimal. If this data ever feeds server-side logic beyond display, a Zod schema parse should be added. For the current read-only display use case this is informational only.

No security findings in the following areas — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed: A01 (path construction uses hardcoded WORKSPACE_ROOT, not user input), A02 (no secrets or sensitive data stored; randomUUID() from Node crypto), A03 (all inputs validated via Zod before use; spawn uses a hardcoded script path with no user-controlled arguments), A06 (no new third-party dependencies introduced), A07 (no auth endpoints; not applicable to this local GUI server), A08 (no deserialization of untrusted data; atomic writes used), A09 (errors logged to stderr only, no stack traces returned to callers), A10 (no server-side URL fetching). CORS restricted to localhost. Security headers applied on all responses (CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy). Body size capped at 1 MiB. UUID fields validated with z.string().uuid() and existence-checked against live registry.

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied: handleGetPersonas() at api-models.ts line 497 used `new ApiError('PARSE_ERROR', ...)` for a malformed name-mapping.json. The error code PARSE_ERROR is not handled by apiErrorToStatus() in server.ts (only NOT_FOUND, FORBIDDEN, VALIDATION_ERROR, CONFLICT are mapped), so this threw HTTP 500 for a malformed JSON file. The identical scenario in handleUpdateAssignments() (line 322) correctly uses VALIDATION_ERROR → 400. Changed to `new ApiError('VALIDATION_ERROR', 'name-mapping.json is not valid JSON.')` for consistency and correct HTTP status semantics. Behavior change: corrupt name-mapping.json now returns 400 instead of 500 from GET /api/personas — this is the correct response since it is a data-integrity problem, not a server failure.

handleUpdateAssignments() reads name-mapping.json and local.json sequentially (await readFile → await readModels). Both reads are independent and could be parallelized with Promise.all() — already noted by Developer. At current scale this is a low-priority optimization, but worth addressing if the model registry grows large or if latency is ever profiled.

The module-level `buildInProgress` flag in api-models.ts is correct for a single-process server but will not scale to a multi-worker scenario (e.g. cluster mode or worker_threads). The current architecture is single-process and this is fine. If multi-worker support is ever added, the concurrency guard must be moved to a shared medium (e.g. a lockfile or atomic rename). Low risk for the current architecture — documented for future awareness.

server.ts handleRequest() has grown to ~1960 lines with 5 additional inline body-parsing route blocks (PUT /api/models, POST /api/models/load-defaults, PUT /api/model-assignments, POST /api/model-assignments/replace, POST /api/personas/rebuild). Each block is identical in structure: readJsonBody → call handler → sendJson → catch ApiError / PayloadTooLargeError. A typed dispatchBodyRoute() helper would eliminate this boilerplate. Out of scope for this WP, but the pattern is now repeated enough that a dedicated refactor WP would be justified.

[documentation-forward] The PersonaEntry interface exported from api-models.ts (lines 470–478) is the public contract for GET /api/personas. The interface is defined but lacks a JSDoc comment explaining what each optional field means (model, model_slug, cc_model, number) and under what conditions they are populated. Add a JSDoc block documenting the optional fields and their semantics for future contributors integrating with this endpoint.

[documentation-forward] The stale flag semantics of GET /api/model-assignments are non-obvious: stale: false when neither user file exists (no build needed), stale: false when only default.json is newer (excluded by design), stale: false when name-mapping.json does not exist. These rules are documented in the computeStale() @internal JSDoc but are not surfaced in the handler-level JSDoc for handleGetAssignments(). Consider adding a brief note on the stale field semantics to the handleGetAssignments() JSDoc to aid frontend consumers.
